title: Writing SSL/TLS inspection exemptions without exempting too much

bypass-only-controlled.statement: Zscaler strongly recommends inspecting all traffic and placing a bypass only for controlled, understood exceptions, and only after consulting legal counsel for the impacted region.

quotes: Zscaler strongly recommends that you inspect all traffic and place a bypass only in controlled and understood exceptions.
Choose to bypass traffic only after consulting your legal counsel for the impacted region.

bypass-purposes.statement: The cases where a bypass is generally applicable are banking and finance destinations, healthcare destinations, business functions that need undecryptable traffic, business functions that need certificate-pinned sites or applications, and applications such as parts of Microsoft 365 that break when inspected.

quotes: Banking and finance destinations.
Healthcare destinations.
Business functions that require the use of undecryptable traffic.
Business functions that require the use of certificate-pinned sites or applications.
Applications, such as certain parts of Microsoft 365, that have issues when inspected.

finance-health-recommendation.statement: Some organizations bypass the Finance and Health URL categories for privacy reasons, but Zscaler recommends enabling inspection for all URL categories.

quotes: Some organizations choose to bypass SSL/TLS Inspection for Finance and Health URL categories due to privacy concerns.
Zscaler recommends that you enable SSL/TLS Inspection for all URL categories.

opt-out-design.statement: Build the rule set as opt-out: end with an Inspect rule for everything not explicitly exempted, so new groups, applications, categories and locations are inspected automatically until configured otherwise.

quotes: Build with the intention of Opt-Out in mind. Set your final policy to inspect everything not explicitly exempted previously.

fqdn-not-ip.statement: Bypass entries should be FQDNs or domains, not IP addresses.

quotes: Avoid adding IP addresses in favor of FQDNs or domains.
Use an FQDN or domains, and avoid exclusion based on IP addresses.

specific-not-wildcard.statement: Prefer the most specific domains over wildcards: add `corp.safemarch.com` and `eng.safemarch.com` rather than `.safemarch.com`.

quotes: While adding domains, try adding the most specific domains in the bypass instead of wildcards

no-paths.statement: A bypass entry must be the FQDN only: anything beyond the domain, such as a path, is not visible without first inspecting the communication.

quotes: Do not add file paths or anything other than the FQDN (i.e., safemarch.com/games/), as anything beyond the domain is not visible without first inspecting the communication.

prefer-cloud-app.statement: Where a matching Cloud Application exists, use it instead of managing the domains by hand.

quotes: Avoid trying to manage domains if a matching Cloud Application exists.

shared-storage-domains.statement: Do not exempt the shared-storage CDN domains `.s3.amazonaws.com`, `.blob.core.windows.net` or `.cloudfront.net` or similar: any subscriber can get its own storage subdomain there, so exempting the parent leaves every AWS S3 or Azure Blob account uninspected.

quotes: (.s3).amazonaws.com
(.blob.core).windows.net
.cloudfront.net
These are destinations where any subscriber can get their own file storage subdomain.
Exempting these domains from inspection means no inspection occurs for any AWS S3 or Azure Blob storage account

exception-hygiene.statement: Keep SSL exceptions in at least one dedicated URL category or destination group, investigate before adding any bypass, and document every entry for later audit.

quotes: Zscaler recommends creating at least one URL category or IP and FQDN Destination Group specific to managing SSL exceptions.
Avoid creating bypasses to resolve access issues without proper investigation and understanding.
Document your entries within your documentation system for future reference during the audit and review.

predefined-exemptions-differ.statement: The two predefined exemption styles differ in what survives: the Zscaler Recommended Exemptions rule is Do Not Inspect with Evaluate Other Policies, so URL Filtering still runs, while the Zscaler Microsoft 365 Click-to-Run rule is Do Not Inspect with Bypass Other Policies, so it does not.
predefined-exemptions-differ.conditions: Read from the guide's example rule table, which is flattened PDF text; the row alignment is the reading used here.

quotes: 1 Zscaler N/A Do Not Inspect Recommended Evaluate Other Exemption Rule Policies Show End User Notifications: Disabled
Click-to-Run (Policy > URL & Cloud Do Not Inspect 3 N/A App Control > Bypass Other Policies

m365-inspect-except-click-to-run.statement: The guide's Microsoft 365 policy is to inspect OneDrive, SharePoint and similar services but exclude Click-to-Run.

quotes: Inspect OneDrive, SharePoint, etc., but exclude Click-to-Run from Microsoft 365.

googleusercontent-exemption.title: Whether a wildcard on googleusercontent.com is as dangerous as the shared-storage CDN domains
googleusercontent-exemption.detail: Unverified legacy statement: '*.googleusercontent.com - Google Drive shared content lives under user-suffixed subdomains' listed with S3, Azure Blob and CloudFront as exemptions to avoid. The guide names only S3, Azure Blob and CloudFront.

click-to-run-rationale.title: Why Microsoft 365 Click-to-Run ships with Bypass Other Policies
click-to-run-rationale.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Zscaler ships Click-to-Run with Bypass Other Policies 'because the URLs would break under URL Filtering too'. The guide shows the rule and its action but gives no reason.
